```{r setup}
source(here::here("R", "00_setup.R"))

tab <- function(name, ...) {
  read_csv(here("output", "tables", paste0(name, ".csv")), show_col_types = FALSE, ...)
}
fig <- function(name) knitr::include_graphics(here("output", "figures", paste0(name, ".png")))
fmt <- function(x) format(round(x), big.mark = ",")

funnel  <- tab("exclusions_03_clean")
type    <- tab("prix_m2_par_type")
zt      <- tab("prix_m2_par_zone_type")
commune <- tab("prix_m2_par_commune", col_types = cols(code_commune = col_character()))
mois    <- tab("prix_m2_par_mois")
stages  <- tab("ventes_par_mois_et_etape")
robust  <- tab("robustesse_parametres")
bornes  <- tab("bornes_prix_m2_exclus")
nature  <- tab("nature_mutation_decembre")

# Numbers quoted in the text, all computed from the tables above.
n_all   <- funnel$n_ventes[1]
n_final <- tail(funnel$n_ventes, 1)
med     <- function(t) type$prix_m2_median[type$type_local == t]
zmed    <- function(z, t) zt$prix_m2_median[zt$zone == z & zt$type_local == t]
zn      <- function(z, t) zt$n_ventes[zt$zone == z & zt$type_local == t]
share_tls <- function(t) zn("Toulouse", t) / sum(zt$n_ventes[zt$type_local == t])

communes_ok <- commune |> filter(n_ventes >= 30)
low  <- communes_ok |> slice_min(prix_m2_median, n = 1)
high <- communes_ok |> slice_max(prix_m2_median, n = 1)

final_col  <- stages$`4_echantillon_final`
dec_ratio  <- final_col[12] / mean(final_col[1:11])
peak_month <- format(mois$mois[which.max(mois$n_ventes)], "%B")
vefa <- nature |> filter(str_starts(nature_mutation, "Vente en l'état"))
vefa_dec <- vefa$part_pct[vefa$periode == "decembre"]
vefa_rest <- vefa$part_pct[vefa$periode == "jan_nov"]

max_all <- max(abs(robust$ecart_median_pct))
max_ens <- max(abs(robust$ecart_median_pct[robust$type_local == "Ensemble"]))
n_low  <- sum(bornes$n_ventes[bornes$cote == "sous le plancher"])
n_high <- sum(bornes$n_ventes[bornes$cote == "au-dessus du plafond"])
```

## Question and main results

What was the price per m² of houses and flats sold in Haute-Garonne in 2025, and how does it differ by dwelling type, location and month?

- The sample is **`r fmt(n_final)` sales** out of `r fmt(n_all)` recorded transactions (`r round(100 * n_final / n_all)`%), each containing exactly one house or flat.
- The median price is **`r fmt(med("Appartement"))` EUR/m² for flats** and **`r fmt(med("Maison"))` EUR/m² for houses**.
- That gap comes from where each type is sold, not from a flat premium: `r round(100 * share_tls("Appartement"))`% of flats but only `r round(100 * share_tls("Maison"))`% of houses are in Toulouse. Within Toulouse houses are more expensive (`r fmt(zmed("Toulouse", "Maison"))` vs `r fmt(zmed("Toulouse", "Appartement"))`); outside Toulouse the two types are almost the same (`r fmt(zmed("Rest of the 31", "Maison"))` vs `r fmt(zmed("Rest of the 31", "Appartement"))`).
- Monthly median prices are flat through the year; sales volumes are not.
- The results move by less than `r ceiling(max_all)`% when any cleaning threshold is changed.

## Data

Source: DVF géolocalisées (Etalab), derived from the DGFiP *Demandes de valeurs foncières*, national file for 2025, filtered to département 31. One row of the raw file is a parcel or a premises, not a sale: the price of the whole sale is repeated on every row. The unit of analysis is therefore the sale (`id_mutation`), and the cleaning works at that level.

## Cleaning

A sale is kept if it is an ordinary sale (*Vente*) of exactly one house or flat, with no professional premises in the same deed, a known price, and a plausible price, surface and price per m². Each step removes sales, and the table shows how many.

```{r funnel}
funnel |>
  transmute(Step = step, `Sales left` = n_ventes, Removed = excluded) |>
  knitr::kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

The thresholds are `prix_min` = `r fmt(prix_min)` EUR, `surface_max` = `r surface_max` m², and price per m² between `r prix_m2_min` and `r fmt(prix_m2_max)` EUR. They come from orders of magnitude of the market, not from the data, which is why the robustness section below varies them.

## Results

### By dwelling type

```{r type}
type |>
  transmute(Type = type_local, Sales = n_ventes, Q1 = prix_m2_q1,
            Median = prix_m2_median, Q3 = prix_m2_q3, `Median surface (m²)` = surface_mediane) |>
  knitr::kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

Medians and quartiles are used instead of means because the distribution of price per m² is right-skewed.

```{r fig-type}
fig("prix_m2_distribution_par_type")
```

### Toulouse against the rest of the département

```{r zone}
zt |>
  transmute(Zone = zone, Type = type_local, Sales = n_ventes,
            `Median EUR/m²` = prix_m2_median, `Median surface (m²)` = surface_mediane) |>
  knitr::kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

This is a descriptive comparison, not an adjusted one: location, size and condition are not controlled for. Houses also include the land, which flats do not, so the two types are not like-for-like.

### By commune

Among communes with at least 30 sales, medians run from about `r fmt(low$prix_m2_median)` EUR/m² (`r low$nom_commune`, `r low$n_ventes` sales) to about `r fmt(high$prix_m2_median)` (`r high$nom_commune`, `r high$n_ventes` sales).

```{r fig-commune}
fig("prix_m2_par_commune")
```

### By month

```{r fig-mois}
fig("prix_m2_par_mois")
```

Monthly medians stay between `r fmt(min(mois$prix_m2_median))` and `r fmt(max(mois$prix_m2_median))` EUR/m². The number of sales ranges from `r fmt(min(mois$n_ventes))` to `r fmt(max(mois$n_ventes))`, with the peak in `r peak_month`. Toulouse's share of monthly sales stays within a narrow band, so the mix between zones does not explain the monthly pattern.

```{r fig-mois-zone}
fig("prix_m2_par_mois_zone")
```

December is the second busiest month in the final sample, `r round(100 * (dec_ratio - 1))`% above the January–November average. In the full file the December excess is larger, and part of it comes from new-build sales (*VEFA*), which are `r vefa_dec`% of December transactions against `r vefa_rest`% in the other months and are excluded by the cleaning. The excess does not disappear after the cleaning, and **I have not established why**: this analysis does not test any explanation.

## Robustness

Each threshold is changed on its own, the other three staying at their baseline value. The largest change in a median, for any type, is `r max_all`%, and for the whole sample `r max_ens`%.

```{r robust}
robust |>
  filter(parametre != "baseline", type_local == "Ensemble") |>
  transmute(Parameter = parametre, Value = valeur, `Sales left` = n_ventes,
            `Change in sales` = ecart_n, `Change in median (%)` = ecart_median_pct) |>
  knitr::kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

The price-per-m² bounds remove `r n_low + n_high` sales: `r n_low` below the floor and `r n_high` above the ceiling.

```{r bornes}
bornes |>
  transmute(Side = cote, Type = type_local, Sales = n_ventes,
            `Median price (EUR)` = prix_median, `Median surface (m²)` = surface_mediane,
            `Median EUR/m²` = prix_m2_median) |>
  knitr::kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

Sales under the floor have a median price of roughly 15,000 to 25,000 EUR, which is not a plausible price for a whole dwelling; they may be partial interests or entry errors. The high side mixes very small surfaces with high prices and a few expensive houses. I did not check these sales one by one.

## Limits

- One year of data, and a description only: no causal claim is made.
- Sales with several dwellings or with professional premises are excluded, so the sample covers simple residential sales and not the whole market.
- The price per m² is the price of the whole sale divided by the built surface. Condition, floor, outbuildings and land are not observed.
- Two identical flats on the same parcel in one sale would count as one dwelling and double the price per m²; the upper bound limits the effect.
- Communes with few sales have unreliable medians, hence the minimum of 30 sales for the commune comparison.

## Reproducing this report

The raw file is not in the repository. Place `full-2025.csv.gz` in `data/raw/`, then run `R/02_filter_31.R`, `R/03_clean.R`, `R/04_describe.R` and `R/05_robustness.R` in this order, and render `report/dvf_report.qmd`.
